question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Macroeconomics - National Income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Income** is a core concept in **macroeconomics**.
 
• **Macroeconomics** focuses on the study of the **economy as a whole**, including large-scale indicators such as **GDP**, **National Income**, and **employment levels**.
 
• **National Income** refers to the **total value of goods and services** produced by a country during a specific period, typically a year.
 
• It includes components like **wages, rents, interests, and profits** generated within an economy.
 
• Macroeconomics analyzes factors like **inflation, unemployment, fiscal policies, and monetary policies**, which are linked to National Income.
 
• Understanding **National Income** helps policymakers and economists to assess the **economic health of a nation** and formulate appropriate policies.
 
• Examples of tools used for measuring National Income include **GDP (Gross Domestic Product)**, **GNP (Gross National Product)**, and **Net National Income (NNI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microeconomics - Inflation rate**__

 __
 
• **Inflation rate** is a concept studied under **macroeconomics**, not microeconomics.
 
• It measures the **rate of increase in prices** of goods and services over a period of time.
 
• **Microeconomics**, on the other hand, focuses on individual market behavior, such as pricing and consumer choices.
 
 
 
• **Macroeconomics - Price of tea**__
 __
 
• The **price of tea** is a specific and localized concept studied under **microeconomics**, as it deals with individual markets and consumer behavior.
 
• **Macroeconomics** deals with broader economic phenomena, not individual product prices.
 
 
 
• **Microeconomics - GDP**__
 
 
• **GDP (Gross Domestic Product)** is a key indicator in **macroeconomics**, as it reflects the overall economic output of a country.
 
• **Microeconomics** focuses on individual-level decision-making, not aggregate measures like GDP.
